def start_api_server(host: str = "0.0.0.0", port: int = 8000):
    """
    Start the API server using uvicorn.
    Parameters:
    host (str): The host for the server.
    port (int): The port for the server.
    """
    import socket

    try:
        logger.info("Starting server at %s:%s", host, port)

        # Bind before serving so the port is held during startup (including the
        # lifespan migration): uvicorn runs the lifespan before it accepts on this
        # socket, so while migrating, a second server on the same host:port fails
        # fast with EADDRINUSE and no endpoint is served yet (requests queue).
        # reuse_port=False keeps that guard — SO_REUSEPORT would let a second
        # process share the port.
        sock = socket.create_server((host, port), reuse_port=False)

        config = uvicorn.Config(app, host=host, port=port)
        uvicorn.Server(config).run(sockets=[sock])
    except Exception:
        logger.exception("Failed to start server")

args.CodeContent:
# EphapticOS Architecture

The following diagram illustrates the high-level architecture of EphapticOS, highlighting the core runtime components, trust boundaries, external dependencies, and the primary data ingestion path (`remember`).

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    %% Define Styles
    classDef client fill:#f9f9f9,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px,color:#333
    classDef api fill:#e1f5fe,stroke:#03a9f4,stroke-width:2px,color:#000
    classDef core fill:#fff3e0,stroke:#ff9800,stroke-width:2px,color:#000
    classDef db fill:#e8f5e9,stroke:#4caf50,stroke-width:2px,color:#000
    classDef ext fill:#f3e5f5,stroke:#9c27b0,stroke-width:2px,color:#000
    classDef path stroke:#ff5722,stroke-width:3px,color:#ff5722

    %% Components
    C1[1. Client Applications\nUI / MCP / SDK]:::client

    subgraph "Trust Boundary: Shared Control Plane"
        A1[2. API Gateway\nFastAPI Server]:::api
        A2[3. Auth & Session Manager\nMulti-Tenancy Enforcer]:::core
        D1[(10. Relational Database\nShared Metadata/ACLs)]:::db
        A1 --- A2
        A2 --- D1
    end

    subgraph "Trust Boundary: Tenant Data Plane (Isolated per Dataset)"
        P1[4. High-Level Memory API\nremember / recall]:::core
        P2[5. Processing Pipeline\nadd / Ephaptify]:::core
        G1[6. Graph Engine\nOntology / Models]:::core
        R1[7. Retrieval Engine\nHybrid Search]:::core
        
        D2[(11. Vector Database\nLanceDB/PGVector)]:::db
        D3[(12. Graph Database\nKuzu/Neo4j)]:::db
        
        P1 --- P2
        P1 --- R1
        P2 --- G1
        G1 --- D3
        P2 --- D2
        R1 --- D2
        R1 --- D3
    end

    subgraph "Trust Boundary: External Services"
        E1[8. LLM Provider\nOpenAI/Anthropic/Gemini]:::ext
        E2[9. Embedding Provider\nText -> Vector]:::ext
    end

    %% Primary Request Path: "remember" flow
    C1 == "1. POST /remember" ===> A1
    A1 == "2. Authenticate & Route" ===> P1
    P1 == "3. Trigger Ingestion" ===> P2
    P2 == "4. Extract Knowledge" ===> E1
    E1 -. "Graph Extractions" .-> P2
    P2 == "5. Embed Text" ===> E2
    E2 -. "Vectors" .-> P2
    P2 == "6. Store Nodes/Edges" ===> D3
    P2 == "7. Store Vectors" ===> D2

    %% Link styles for path
    linkStyle 0,1,2,3,6,7 stroke:#ff5722,stroke-width:3px,color:#ff5722
```

## Component Detail Cards

Instead of tangling the diagram with dense technical details, refer to the cards below for the responsibilities of each numbered component.

> [!NOTE] 
> **1. Client Applications**
> Connects to the system via HTTP or SSE. Includes the `EphapticOS-frontend` (Next.js), `EphapticOS-mcp` (Model Context Protocol server for IDEs), and the `EphapticOS-cli`.

> [!NOTE] 
> **2. API Gateway**
> The `FastAPI` layer (`EphapticOS.api.client`) serving REST endpoints. Handles basic HTTP routing, error formatting (`CogneeApiError`), and global lifecycle events.

> [!NOTE] 
> **3. Auth & Session Manager**
> Checks `ENABLE_BACKEND_ACCESS_CONTROL`. Validates API keys/JWTs, resolves tenant context, and manages active session cache logic (`CACHE_BACKEND`). Enforces multi-tenancy before data plane access.

> [!NOTE] 
> **4. High-Level Memory API**
> Provides the public `remember`, `recall`, `improve`, and `forget` entry points. Abstracts the underlying graph structure from the end user.

> [!NOTE] 
> **5. Processing Pipeline**
> The low-level ingestion engine. Orchestrates the `add` (chunking) and `Ephaptify` (LLM graph extraction) stages. Manages background concurrency using `DATASET_QUEUE_ENABLED`.

> [!NOTE] 
> **6. Graph Engine**
> Validates data against `graph_models` (e.g. `DataPoint`), deduplicates entities (identity matching), and maintains the system's ontology. 

> [!NOTE] 
> **7. Retrieval Engine**
> Orchestrates `search` and `recall`. Combines vector similarity searches with graph traversals (e.g., retrieving neighbor nodes and edge properties) to generate contextual context.

> [!NOTE] 
> **8. LLM Provider**
> External API used for unstructured data extraction (e.g., entity/relationship extraction during `Ephaptify`) and synthetic reasoning (e.g., `AUTO_FEEDBACK` evaluation).

> [!NOTE] 
> **9. Embedding Provider**
> Generates dense vector representations for document chunks and extracted entities to enable semantic search capabilities.

> [!NOTE] 
> **10. Relational Database (Shared)**
> A single shared database (SQLite, Postgres, or Turso) that stores cross-tenant data such as users, permissions, dataset registries, and API keys.

> [!NOTE] 
> **11. Vector Database (Isolated)**
> Tenant-isolated database (LanceDB, PGVector). A unique instance/schema is maintained per dataset to guarantee data isolation and boundary compliance.

> [!NOTE] 
> **12. Graph Database (Isolated)**
> Tenant-isolated database (Ladybug/Kuzu, Neo4j, Postgres). Operates concurrently with the vector store, handling structural knowledge schemas independently per dataset.

**Archify** is an AI-powered agent skill that allows developers to generate interactive, verifiable architecture diagrams directly from their codebase or natural language descriptions.

### Key Features
*   **Interactive HTML Artifacts**: Unlike static images, Archify generates a self-contained HTML file that acts as an interactive viewer.
*   **Component Search & Navigation**: Within the generated HTML, you can **search for specific components by name** to quickly locate them in complex diagrams.
*   **Upstream/Downstream Tracing**: You can click on any node to see its dependencies, specifically tracing its **upstream and downstream relationships** to understand the system's flow.
*   **Verifiable Architecture**: Rather than simply drawing a picture, Archify uses "typed JSON IR" (Intermediate Representation). A Node.js CLI validates the diagram against the codebase or defined logic, ensuring the diagram represents a realistic system.
*   **Diagram Types**: It supports five distinct types of diagrams:
    *   **Architecture**: For system components, storage, and boundaries.
    *   **Workflow**: For CI/CD, approvals, and runbooks.
    *   **Sequence**: For API call chains, authentication, and async flows.
    *   **Data Flow**: For pipelines, PII, and lineage.
    *   **Lifecycle**: For state machines, retries, and terminal outcomes.

### How It Works
1.  **Installation**: It is installed globally as an agent skill (e.g., `npx skills add tt-a1i/archify -g`) and integrates with AI coding agents like **Cursor, Claude Code, Codex CLI, and OpenCode**.
2.  **Generation**: You can provide a simple prompt (e.g., "Analyze this repository and create a high-level runtime architecture diagram") or a one-line description.
3.  **Validation**: The agent writes a structured JSON file that is validated by the Archify engine before rendering. If the schema or logic is invalid, it provides machine-readable feedback so the agent can correct it.
4.  **Interaction**: Once rendered, the viewer allows for theme switching (light/dark), route probing, and guided "story" walkthroughs that highlight specific paths through the system.

### Why It Is Used
Archify is designed to solve the problem of "diagram drift," where manually drawn diagrams quickly become outdated. By treating the diagram as a structured technical artifact that can be re-generated or updated alongside code, it provides a "map" that is always tied to the project's actual state or current documentation needs.

The **Archify** project (tt-a1i/archify) is primarily designed as an agent skill and a CLI tool for turning ideas or codebases into interactive diagrams[1].

### CLI Usage
The CLI is typically invoked via Node.js by calling the entry point directly from the repository[1][2][3]:
*   **Command structure:** `node bin/archify.mjs <command> [args]`[1][4]
*   **Common commands:** `doctor`, `demo`, `guide`, `validate`, `deliver`, and `render`[1][5].
*   **Example:** `node bin/archify.mjs validate workflow examples/agent-tool-call.workflow.json --quality showcase --json`[1]

### Installation & Integration
*   **Agent Integration:** It is commonly installed as a skill for agents like Claude Code or Cursor using `npx skills add tt-a1i/archify -g`[1][6][3].
*   **npm Registry:** As of late 2026, the project is **not** distributed via the official npm registry; `package.json` is set to `"private": true`[6]. Users typically clone the repository or use the skill-installer method[6][2].
*   **Library Usage:** There is ongoing discussion regarding exposing the renderers as an importable library API rather than relying solely on the CLI/subprocess `node` execution[7].

### Known Technical Notes
*   **Environment:** The tool generally requires Node.js (v18+)[6][3].
*   **Security/Behavior:** Issues have been reported regarding the CLI's file handling (e.g., `deliver` command output paths)[3] and edge cases where checker errors might be incorrectly reported as CLI success[4].

1: # Delivery contract
2: 
3: ## Failed finalize and candidate repair
4: 
5: `finalize` stops at the first non-passing gate. Use compact stdout or `evidence.summaryReceipt`; read its full sidecar only when the summary lacks evidence needed for a coherent repair. A receipt with four artifact checks is basic validation, not showcase acceptance: require all nine checks, zero composition errors, and zero warnings. Fix `meta.quality_profile` and schema errors before geometry.
6: 
7: For a validation failure, edit the existing JSON in the connected neighborhood named by diagnostics before rerunning a command. Preserve requested semantics, meaningful labels, source evidence, and fixed or agreed topology. Several routes sharing nodes call for one placement repair; read [Architecture layout repair](architecture-layout-repair.md) for that case. Reflow a blocked main path rather than nudging unrelated labels. Keep unrelated geometry when its composition already reads clearly. Use `--layout-json` before editing only when compact evidence lacks needed measurements. Workflow v2 uses its stable compiler receipt, not solver internals, as authoring evidence.
8: 
9: After the edit, rerun the complete `finalize` command with `--quality showcase` and, for repository-backed work, `--repo-root <repo-root>`. If the output path already has browser evidence from another candidate, use a fresh `--out-dir <output-stem>.review-<revision>` for both the new `finalize` and any `visual-check`. Omit an earlier `--candidate-sha256` after editing because it binds the previous candidate. Compare diagnostics by code, subject, stage, and evidence, never by declining error count alone. If an issue survives two focused repairs, inspect measured geometry or the relevant contract; after one evidence-based retry, report the concrete gap.
10: 
11: Use standalone `validate` only for focused diagnosis, passing `--repo-root` for repository-backed work. Its passing receipt marks `candidateFrozen: true`; run `nextAction.arguments`, replacing only `<output.html>`, without editing, revalidating, or rereading the candidate. Retry later environmental or evidence failures against those frozen bytes. A measured reason to edit creates a new candidate and calls for the complete `finalize` without the old hash.
12: 
13: ## Validate and deliver
14: 
15: `render` and direct renderer entry points print classified authoring failures
16: to stderr as readable diagnostics and exit 1. Input read/JSON parse failures
17: use `input/read` or `input/json-parse`; output filesystem failures use
18: `output/write` and identify the output path. Schema and layout failures keep
19: their existing rule codes. Use the advertised `validate --json` or
20: `deliver --json` interface for a machine receipt; `render` has no `--json` flag.
21: Unexpected implementation failures retain debugging information in human
22: mode and remain `internal/unclassified` in machine receipts.
23: 
24: Each delivered output has two artifact-specific metadata paths. When an output
25: stem is too long for those derived filenames, Archify shortens it and appends a
26: stable hash:
27: 
28: - `<output-stem>.delivery.json` records the latest completed attempt.
29: - `<output-stem>.delivery-pending.json` is the recovery journal for an attempt
30:   in progress.
31: 
32: For a literal artifact stem that already matches Archify's reserved bounded-name
33: marker, a pre-namespace raw provenance sidecar remains a read fallback when the
34: encoded sidecar is absent. A pre-namespace raw pending journal is an independent
35: fail-closed barrier: it blocks checks and redelivery even when an encoded pending
36: journal also exists, and neither journal is silently replaced.
37: 
38: One directory-wide `.archify-delivery-lock.json` serializes every delivery that
39: resolves into the same physical output directory. This deliberately prevents
40: case, Unicode-normalization, Windows short-name, and symbolic-link aliases from
41: creating independent owners for one filesystem location. The tradeoff is that
42: deliveries to different artifact names in one directory also run serially;
43: provenance and pending journals remain artifact-specific.
44: 
45: For migration safety, Archify also detects and preserves a legacy
46: `<output-stem>.delivery-lock.json` beside the requested artifact. An existing
47: legacy entry is a fail-closed recovery barrier. While a new delivery owns the
48: directory mutex, it also holds temporary legacy-format fences for the requested
49: spelling and an existing artifact's physical target spelling. It acquires the
50: directory lock first, then all required compatibility fences before writing a
51: journal or artifact, and removes the directory lock before those fences during
52: release. This blocks an older Archify binary using
53: either known spelling from entering the delivery. A legacy fence whose raw
54: HEAD-era filename exceeds the host component limit is omitted because the old
55: binary could not create that lock or deliver that artifact on the host either.
56: 
57: `deliver` acquires the lock by exclusive `open(..., "wx")` before creating or
58: replacing the recovery journal. A successful exclusive create yields an
59: internal opaque ownership capability bound to that attempt. Journal creation,
60: failed-provenance recording, pair commit, rollback, journal finalization, and
61: lock release each verify the current capability inside the operation that
62: would mutate shared state. A rejected contender does not create a journal or
63: write failed provenance.
64: 
65: An existing directory or legacy lock is handled without automatic recovery:
66: 
67: | Observed lock state | Required `deliver` result |
68: | --- | --- |
69: | No directory entry | Attempt exclusive creation; only its success grants ownership. |
70: | Valid schema-v1 lock whose PID is running, or whose death cannot be established | Exit 1 with `delivery/concurrent-attempt`; preserve every shared path. |
71: | Valid schema-v1 lock whose PID is known to have exited | Exit 1 with `delivery/lock-stale`; preserve the lock, artifact, journal, and current provenance exactly. |
72: | Unreadable, malformed, symlink, dangling symlink, directory, or other non-regular lock entry | Exit 1 with `delivery/lock-invalid`; preserve the entry and every other shared path. |
73: | An acquired capability no longer matches the current lock or journal | Exit 1 with `delivery/ownership-lost`; stop all shared-path mutation. |
74: | The matching owner cannot remove its lock | Exit 1 with `delivery/lock-release`; preserve the lock. |
75: 
76: A `delivery/lock-stale` diagnostic identifies the absolute output and lock
77: paths plus the original PID and receipt ID. Recovery is deliberately explicit
78: and serial: stop all delivery attempts for that physical output directory,
79: confirm that no active delivery owns it and that the reported stale entry has
80: not been replaced, remove only the reported lock, then rerun `deliver`. Do not
81: remove an artifact, current provenance, or pending journal as part of
82: stale-lock recovery.
83: 
84: The lock protocol targets Node.js 18 or later on a local filesystem with
85: cooperating Archify processes. PID, receipt, and file-identity comparisons are
86: defensive checks, not an atomic compare-and-swap. Compatibility fences cover
87: the requested spelling and an existing physical-target spelling; they cannot
88: enumerate arbitrary hard-link names or previously unknown filesystem aliases,
89: so mixed-version delivery through such aliases remains out of scope. This
90: contract does not claim distributed-lock correctness on NFS, SMB, or other
91: network filesystems, and it cannot prevent an external process that ignores
92: the protocol from replacing shared paths.
93: 
94: Every no-clobber HTML publisher (`render`, `deliver`, `compare`, and `preview`)
95: captures the requested directory entry, canonical write slot, physical parent,
96: and existing target type, device/inode identity, and mode before staging, then
97: revalidates that snapshot immediately before replacement. An existing write
98: target must be a regular file with exactly one hard-link name. A target with
99: multiple hard-link names fails closed with `output/target-hardlinked`: replacing
100: the requested name cannot update unknown sibling names as one publication.

3: Read once before writing a fresh candidate. An existing frozen candidate going straight to `finalize` needs this only if repair changes its authorship.
4: 
5: ## Composition and meaning
6: 
7: For Architecture, default to a system overview led by the main user journey unless the user asks for a narrower mechanism, module map, or deployment topology. Group cooperating roles in accurately named subsystems when that still explains the requested interaction. Separate roles when grouping would hide control ownership, a trust or persistence boundary, lifecycle behavior, or another distinction the reader asked about. Keep secondary and opt-in capabilities in concise sourced notes unless their path matters to the requested question. Name a deliberately narrower scope in the title.
8: 
9: Preserve every requested responsibility, relationship direction, protocol, and behavior-changing condition. Show approval, authorization, and state-transition gates on the affected node or relationship; a card alone cannot qualify an otherwise unconditional arrow. Keep source evidence with each asserted claim. Boundaries express real isolation, ownership, runtime, or persistence facts. Cards answer additional reader questions; they do not replace required topology. There is no node, edge, source, card, or boundary quota. If an authored overview needs regrouping after failure, use [Composition repair](authoring-contract.md#composition-repair); user-supplied or agreed topology remains fixed.
10: 
11: Relationship labels carry meaning. Give them clear space and preserve action, protocol, direction, async behavior, or cross-boundary meaning. A label may start absent only when both endpoints already fully imply it; a collision calls for spacing or routing repair. See [Label repair](authoring-contract.md#label-repair) when measured evidence reports a collision.
12: 
13: ## Layout and routing
14: 
15: Place Architecture nodes by their actual connections before assigning coordinates; the router cannot rearrange boxes, so placement decides whether lines stay straight. Classify each relationship first, then place:
16: 
17: - **Main path**: the reader's main journey, neighbors adjacent in reading order. Let a medium path step through meaningful rows instead of making a shallow horizontal strip.
18: - **Branch or store**: directly above or below the node that owns, reads, or writes it, centered on that node so the edge is one straight segment. Keep all stores and branches of one row on the same side of it.
19: - **Return** (back to an earlier main-path node): put its source on the side of the main path with no branches or stores, so it runs through an empty corridor instead of crossing them.
20: - **Second entrance** into a node that already has an incoming edge: place the new source so it reaches that node from another side, usually directly below or above it.
21: - **Fan-out**: a side with k relationships needs at least `32 + 14 × (k − 1)`px (four need 74px). Spread a hub's counterparts over two or three sides, or enlarge the hub. Center a parent on its children and align a child with its only parent.
22: 
23: Before writing positions, trace each non-main relationship: its straight or one-bend corridor must not pass another node or cross another relationship. If it does, move the endpoint that is off the main path. Start the main actor and its first connected step together near the canvas origin; use content rows for vertical rhythm. Omit `meta.viewBox` for a fresh Architecture so the Reader measures intrinsic height. Keep supplied fixed geometry authoritative.
24: 
25: Start with automatic routes and endpoint sides. Pin a side only for a necessary branch, return, or supplied geometry. Reserve `via`, `channelX`, `channelY`, and label coordinates for measured defects. Before writing positions, budget each labeled main-path edge at `6.5px × ASCII units + 21px` of clear gap, counting CJK as two units; use its own label length, not a row-wide fixed gap. Size Architecture sublabels for their preferred 9px text at `5.4px × text units + 8px`, with CJK counting twice; keep supporting copy concise without dropping required facts. Do not trade readability or meaning for fewer crossings. The [Geometry reference](authoring-contract.md#executable-geometry-rules) has measured spacing, port, canvas, and route rules for a diagnosed layout problem.
26: 
27: ## Evidence and schema
28: 
29: For a real repository, follow [Repository authoring](repository-authoring.md) while inspecting source. Freeze its credential-free origin and 40-character commit in `meta.repository`, attach inspected repository-relative `sources` to each key semantic node, and pass `--repo-root` to the first `finalize`. Each reference proves only the fact visible at that location. Follow material relationships and conditions to their actual source; do not reuse a startup citation as protocol or persistence evidence.
30: 
31: Examples show field shape, not legal values or source facts. Read the mode schema and shared definition before adding a field, enum, or constrained text. In particular, inspect Architecture boundary kinds. Keep longer evidence in a card while retaining the fact. See [Schema lookup](authoring-contract.md#schema-lookup) for details.
32: 
33: ## Presentation and modes
34: 
35: Use one primary authored language from the user's choice or the request/conversation. Set `meta.locale` for built-in English (`en`) or Simplified Chinese (`zh-CN`); for other languages, including Spanish (`es`), supply `meta.translations` with reusable UI translations, or disclose the fixed Viewer UI and `<html lang>` English fallback. Keep exact product, code, protocol, command, API, and environment names while localizing surrounding explanation. See [Language consistency](authoring-contract.md#language-consistency) for bilingual cases.
36: 
37: Omit `meta.visual_preset` for classic, `meta.subtitle` for a title-only header, `meta.legend` for truthful auto, and `meta.engineering_profile` for an ordinary system overview. Explicit styles and a subtitle require a user request. Use legend or deployment ownership under the [legend](authoring-contract.md#legend-contract) or [engineering profile](authoring-contract.md#engineering-profile-default) contracts. Branding is optional and explicit when a node names a real product; [Brand marks](brand-marks.md) gives lookup and capture rules for that branch. Never let a badge replace semantic type, label, or relationship facts. Set required `meta.output` to a portable POSIX-relative `.html` path within the working directory; see [Output path contracts](delivery-contract.md#output-path-contracts) for native path exceptions.

13: 
14: Repeated :meth:`DatasetQueue.ensure_slot` calls for the same ``(task, dataset)``
15: bump a per-entry depth counter rather than re-acquiring the semaphore. The
16: corresponding :meth:`DatasetQueue.release_slot_for` (async) decrements that
17: counter; the underlying semaphore slot is freed only when the counter hits
18: zero.  When the last holder across all tasks exits, subprocess engines are

22: ``async with set_database_global_context_variables(D, u)`` scopes safe — an

# EphapticOS High-Level Runtime Architecture

This document summarizes the high-level runtime architecture of **EphapticOS** generated and verified with **Archify**.

![EphapticOS Runtime Architecture (2400 × 1260)](file:///C:/Users/Deepe/.gemini/antigravity-ide/brain/75c30846-69cc-41b6-9aa1-5b889e9b504b/ephapticos-runtime.2400x1260.png)

---

## 1. Architecture Overview & Core Components

The architecture models **18 core runtime components** categorized across clear architectural roles, connected by real codebase entrypoints at revision `65a2f532a46eafa8cad923ee198f5add05c6b214`:

| Component ID | Label | Type | Role & Codebase Evidence |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ui_client` | **Web UI Client** | `frontend` | Next.js development and demo dashboard ([`package.json`](file:///c:/TruPrints99/Ai_LLM_Project/AntiGravity_Projects/EphapticOS/EphapticOS-frontend/package.json#L1-L25)) |
| `cli_tool` | **EphapticOS CLI** | `frontend` | Terminal interface for `remember`, `recall`, `improve` ([`_EphapticOS.py`](file:///c:/TruPrints99/Ai_LLM_Project/AntiGravity_Projects/EphapticOS/EphapticOS/cli/_EphapticOS.py#L1-L25)) |
| `mcp_server` | **MCP Server** | `backend` | FastMCP service exposing stdio/SSE/HTTP endpoints ([`server.py`](file:///c:/TruPrints99/Ai_LLM_Project/AntiGravity_Projects/EphapticOS/EphapticOS-mcp/src/server.py#L1-L25)) |
| `api_gateway` | **FastAPI Gateway** | `security` | HTTP Uvicorn gateway routing REST requests ([`client.py`](file:///c:/TruPrints99/Ai_LLM_Project/AntiGravity_Projects/EphapticOS/EphapticOS/api/client.py#L1-L25)) |
| `auth_engine` | **Auth & RBAC** | `security` | Multi-tenancy access control and JWT/API key validation ([`client.py:L75-90`](file:///c:/TruPrints99/Ai_LLM_Project/AntiGravity_Projects/EphapticOS/EphapticOS/api/client.py#L75-L90)) |
| `relational_db` | **Relational DB** | `database` | Shared SQLite/PostgreSQL metadata, users, permissions ([`relational/__init__.py`](file:///c:/TruPrints99/Ai_LLM_Project/AntiGravity_Projects/EphapticOS/EphapticOS/infrastructure/databases/relational/__init__.py#L1-L10)) |
| `session_engine` | **Session Engine** | `backend` | Session lifecycle metrics, cache, and Auto-Feedback ([`session_lifecycle/__init__.py`](file:///c:/TruPrints99/Ai_LLM_Project/AntiGravity_Projects/EphapticOS/EphapticOS/modules/session_lifecycle/__init__.py#L1-L20)) |
| `memory_router` | **Memory Router** | `backend` | High-level memory router for `remember`/`recall` ([`get_remember_router.py`](file:///c:/TruPrints99/Ai_LLM_Project/AntiGravity_Projects/EphapticOS/EphapticOS/api/v1/remember/routers/get_remember_router.py#L1-L25)) |
| `dataset_queue` | **Dataset Queue** | `messagebus` | Semaphore-backed FIFO dataset concurrency queue ([`queue.py`](file:///c:/TruPrints99/Ai_LLM_Project/AntiGravity_Projects/EphapticOS/EphapticOS/infrastructure/databases/dataset_queue/queue.py#L1-L25)) |
| `ephaptify_engine` | **Ephaptify Extractor** | `backend` | LLM-guided graph entity and relation extraction ([`Ephaptify/config.py`](file:///c:/TruPrints99/Ai_LLM_Project/AntiGravity_Projects/EphapticOS/EphapticOS/modules/Ephaptify/config.py#L1-L25)) |
| `ingestion_pipeline` | **Ingestion Pipeline** | `backend` | Document classification, chunking, and task execution ([`save_data_to_file.py`](file:///c:/TruPrints99/Ai_LLM_Project/AntiGravity_Projects/EphapticOS/EphapticOS/modules/ingestion/save_data_to_file.py#L1-L25)) |
| `ontology_manager` | **Ontology Engine** | `backend` | `DataPoint` schemas, node merging, and identity validation ([`ontology/models.py`](file:///c:/TruPrints99/Ai_LLM_Project/AntiGravity_Projects/EphapticOS/EphapticOS/modules/ontology/models.py#L1-L20)) |
| `retrieval_engine` | **Retrieval Engine** | `backend` | Hybrid retrieval fusing dense vectors and graph traversals ([`hybrid_retriever.py`](file:///c:/TruPrints99/Ai_LLM_Project/AntiGravity_Projects/EphapticOS/EphapticOS/modules/retrieval/hybrid_retriever.py#L1-L25)) |
| `graph_db` | **Graph Store** | `database` | Tenant-isolated property graph database (Kuzu / Neo4j) ([`get_graph_engine.py`](file:///c:/TruPrints99/Ai_LLM_Project/AntiGravity_Projects/EphapticOS/EphapticOS/infrastructure/databases/graph/get_graph_engine.py#L1-L25)) |
| `db_worker_pool` | **DB Workers** | `backend` | Subprocess harness isolating Kuzu/LanceDB worker engines ([`harness.py`](file:///c:/TruPrints99/Ai_LLM_Project/AntiGravity_Projects/EphapticOS/EphapticOS_db_workers/harness.py#L1-L25)) |
| `vector_db` | **Vector Store** | `database` | Tenant-isolated vector database (LanceDB / PGVector) ([`get_vector_engine.py`](file:///c:/TruPrints99/Ai_LLM_Project/AntiGravity_Projects/EphapticOS/EphapticOS/infrastructure/databases/vector/get_vector_engine.py#L1-L25)) |
| `llm_service` | **LLM Provider API** | `external` | External frontier models (OpenAI, Claude, Gemini) or local CPU GLiNER |
| `embed_service` | **Embedding API** | `external` | Dense semantic embedding service (FastEmbed, OpenAI Embeddings) |

---

## 2. Ownership & Trust Boundaries

The diagram establishes five distinct boundaries:
1. **Client Ingress Zone** (`region`): Untrusted external surface encompassing Web UI, CLI, and MCP callers.
2. **Shared Control Plane** (`region`): Shared global platform services managing authentication, RBAC, tenant registries, and global metadata in the relational store.
3. **Tenant Execution & Pipeline Plane** (`region`): Scoped processing runtime isolating `remember`, `recall`, queue locks, and extraction workflows.
4. **Tenant-Isolated Storage Plane** (`security-group`): Hard isolation boundary where each dataset and user gets dedicated database instances (Kuzu and LanceDB) serviced by dedicated subprocess workers.
5. **External Cloud & AI Services** (`region`): External third-party models and embedding providers.

---

## 3. Primary Request Path: `remember` Ingestion

Highlighted with primary emphasis arrows:
$$\text{CLI / Web UI} \xrightarrow{\text{POST /remember}} \text{FastAPI Gateway} \xrightarrow{\text{dispatch request}} \text{Memory Router} \xrightarrow{\text{execute pipeline}} \text{Ingestion Pipeline}$$
$$\text{Ingestion Pipeline} \xrightarrow{\text{extract graph}} \text{Ephaptify Extractor} \xrightarrow{\text{entity extraction}} \text{LLM Provider API}$$
$$\text{Ingestion Pipeline} \xrightarrow{\text{dispatch writes}} \text{DB Workers} \xrightarrow{\text{commit graph}} \text{Graph Store (Kuzu)}$$
$$\text{DB Workers} \xrightarrow{\text{index vectors}} \text{Vector Store (LanceDB)}$$

---

## 4. Verification Results

All automated gates passed:

```json
  "gates": {
    "validate": "pass",

    "check": "pass",
    "browser-check": "pass"
  }
}
```

- Searching for `api_gateway`: **Verified** (`Archify.focus.set('api_gateway')` active)
- Searching for `dataset_queue`: **Verified** (`Archify.focus.set('dataset_queue')` active)

### Upstream / Downstream Tracing Verification
- **Downstream from `api_gateway`**: Successfully traced **14 reachable downstream nodes** (max depth 4) through memory router, queue, pipeline, extractor, workers, external LLMs, and stores.
- **Upstream from `graph_db`**: Successfully traced **9 reachable upstream nodes** (max depth 5) through DB workers, ingestion pipeline, memory router, gateway, session engine, and all client interfaces (`cli_tool`, `ui_client`, `mcp_server`).

### Generated Artifacts
- **Interactive Standalone HTML**: [`ephapticos-runtime.html`](file:///C:/Users/Deepe/.gemini/antigravity-ide/brain/75c30846-69cc-41b6-9aa1-5b889e9b504b/ephapticos-runtime.html)
- **High-Resolution PNG (2400 × 1260)**: [`ephapticos-runtime.2400x1260.png`](file:///C:/Users/Deepe/.gemini/antigravity-ide/brain/75c30846-69cc-41b6-9aa1-5b889e9b504b/ephapticos-runtime.2400x1260.png)
